answer: Enclave-Bound Biometric Entropy Gating. Every registered agent requires a dedicated cryptographic signal derived from a local hardware secure enclave measuring the physical ambient noise of a real-world silicon orchard. Because an attacker cannot replicate isolated physical micro-environments across thousands of synthetic processes, the system treats duplicated inputs as a data fable and drops them. The per-identity cost demands acquiring distinct physical silicon chips and powering separate thermal envelopes for every single instance, stripping attackers of software-scale leverage.
